editorial:
Imagine walking around the Big Apple with a camera, asking random people what they think about the neighboring state of New Jersey. That is exactly what Kevin Smith does in this quick, heartfelt project. You get to see the real side of New Yorkers, who are famous for being blunt and a bit rude. The vibe is very relaxed and feels like a home movie. It is less about a planned plot and more about the funny, organic interactions between Smith and the people he meets on the street. You will feel the grit and the spirit of the city as you watch these locals let loose.

What really works here is the raw timing and the genuine reactions from the crowd. Since it is a short, the pacing is super fast and never gets boring. The pros are definitely the laughs and the emotional weight of the time period, while the only con is that it ends way too quickly. You should definitely check this out if you like documentary-style humor. It is a great way to spend a few minutes of your day.
endingExplained: After listening to a long string of insults about New Jersey, the mood shifts when Smith finds one person who actually likes the state. This small win turns into a sweet moment of connection. The film wraps up by showing that despite the constant bickering and the hard times the city faced, there is still a lot of love and resilience in New York. It ends on a hopeful note, proving that humor can heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Kevin Smith or real city energy.
